x: In the Youths' Medley Relay, our team of Bruce, Briggs, Lewis and Sexton, ran away from the opposition and put up a really fine show for juniors.

Dick Negus made a good start by winning the 100 Yards, although Sexton of the School was only beaten by inches. The latter showed good form in winning the 220 Yards, and has now joined the Club, a must useful addition to our ranks.
It was a very closely contested match and the result was decided on the result of the Relay race. Alan Sexton, now running for his school, beat Dick Negus in the 100, and also won the 220 Yards.

Included on the same programme were two Club Junior Handicaps, and with two heats in the 220 Yards the following qualified for the final : Sexton, A.
In the heats of the 4 x 110 Yards Relay, our team of Negus, Cook, Lewis and Sexton, were second and they finished third in the final, a very fine effort.
Sexton and S.
Alan Sexton beat Janner in the 100 yards in 10.4 secs., and the two Bishop brothers, Eric and Len, were first home in the 880. Arthur Bruce won the 1 mile event with Eddie Short second, and Geoff.
Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races.

In the Junior 4 x 110 yards relay our team comprising: Marshall, Tebbutt, Rae and Sexton, in that order, won their heat in 45,5 secs. In the final they drew lane 4, on the outside, and thanks to an almost super human effort by Alan Sexton, after bad baton handling earlier, won in 45.3 secs.
Sexton, 23.0 sec. Sexton won his first heat in 24.1; Tebbutt won his first heat in 24.6; Picton, Marshall and Rae were each second in their heats.

100 yards: 1st, Lowers, 10.5 secs. 220 yards: 1st, Sexton, 23.4 secs. 440 yards: 1st, Cope, 53.6 secs.; 3rd, Underwood. 880 yards: 1st, Marchant 1 min. 59.5 secs.; 3rd, A.
The Club has met with successes in many open meetings and our team of Walker, Sexton, Beaumont and Underwood won the Mile Medley Relay at the Charlotteville meeting on Whit-Monday.
Merrett, with Lowers second and Alan Sexton third. In the 100 yards (under 19) we only had five runners and Frank Kemp was the winner in the good time of 10.4 seconds.

Alan Sexton showed a return to form when he won the 220 yards, with Geoff Osmin in third place. Ian Badiali was runner-up in the 440 yards, and in the one mile we saw Len Herbert and Bill Lucas outstride the opposition to come home together in first place.
The 100 yards saw a new title-holder in Frank Craft, who has now gone to Australia, worse luck, and he beat " Ginger " Holtum, with Alan Sexton in third place.

In the former event we were in the "A" section of the race with such clubs as Poly H., Achilles, Walton, Herne Hill, and Southgate H., and our team of Jack Brown, Holtum, Sexton, and Badiali did well to gain third place.
Holtum, Benstead, Sexton and Basil Walden also gained 3rd place in the Senior 4 x 110 yards relay when this was held at the Brockman meeting on May 24th.
The 220 yards saw Sexton and Merrett running for the Club, and with the 1st two only qualifying, Alan was 3rd in his heat, but Denis came 2nd in his, and so got through to the semi-finals.

Unfortunately, owing to holidays, etc., we were minus the services of Walden and Holtum, and as both Sexton and Bartlett were required for the 4 x 440, it was decided not to field a team for the sprint relay.
Alan Sexton won the Senior 100 yards in 10.3s. and the 220 yards in 22.8secs. Roy Glen was 3rd in the 440 yards and also competed in the shot and discus.
